reset()/imageData lifetime fix: the original called `const imageData = ctx.createImageData(width, height)` ONCE at top level immediately after the first reset(). Two failures followed. (1) A container reporting zero width at first layout made createImageData throw IndexSizeError, and because the throw was top-level the subsequent `animate()` call never ran — the simulation was permanently dead on that load, not merely unseeded; the resize listener then re-ran reset() successfully, so the canvas sized correctly and still nothing drew. (2) On any resize, reset() reallocated `grid`/`nextGrid` to the new dimensions while `imageData` retained the old ones, so the render loop wrote into a buffer of the wrong size. Fixed by declaring `let imageData` and reallocating it inside reset() alongside the grid, and by flooring both dimensions with Math.max(64, ...) so a zero-width parent cannot throw at all. This is the same repair welded_fields already carried at lines 249-265, whose comment 'reallocated with the grid, unlike the original' names this exact defect; the correction is now applied to the original rather than only annotated beside it. Verified in-browser after the fix: canvas 490x316, 25793 lit pixels, animation running, zero console errors.

apps.title: Welded Asteroids
apps.description: The closed-loop stigmergic field itself, living on the quotient surfaces of the topology game: physarum agents, trail and agent-deposited momentum all obey the surface's gluing rule. Six tour levels bind surface + parameter presets + a beta_1 target; 18 declared sliders drive the physarum; the asteroids game survives as a hidden Easter egg (X when beta_1 >= 42). v2.0.1: seam crossings now transform position AND heading together (topo-asteroids flipP protocol — fixes agents stranding at the Klein/projective seams); sim square letterboxed to true 1:1 (fixes stretched height map). v2.1.0: the real fix for the Klein seam-wall — three compounding defects. (1) foldRead/momRead/uvOf mirrored the WRONG axis (topo.y.flip='x' names the axis that mirrors; the code mirrored the other one), so agent sensing disagreed with deposits. (2) Diffusion sampled neighbors with plain torus wrap; on a mirrored identification the flux at the seam never cancels and mass was slowly pumped into the two seam rows — the minutes-scale accumulator. Now neighbor sampling honors the gluing rule (mirrored cell across a mirrored seam) for trail AND momentum, with the vector's mirrored component sign-flipping. (3) Sense samples crossing a mirrored seam have swapped left/right meaning relative to the agent's square frame; the turn rule now swaps L/R when the front and a flank read different fold images — near-seam agents no longer turn back into the seam. Also fixed: wrapPos wrap-count for negative coordinates (floor division) and double-flip when a y-fold pushed x out of range. Verified: 150s Klein soak — no seam wall, no edge pinning; torus/projective/Mobius 45s soaks all stable. v2.2.0: the height map projects the topology — 3D vertices displace along their base normal by the folded trail height (ridges = built loops, valleys = evaporated field), texture texels fold so the parametrization shows the true pullback at every seam, contour lines and agent points ride the same displaced surface, and a '3D relief' slider (0..1) controls the amplitude. Lit MeshStandardMaterial with key/rim lights so relief reads as form. v2.3.0: color separation + seam-continuous contours. Chemical field stays green; contour overlays recolored to the violet family; agents drawn as cyan-white dots (2D overlay + 3D points) so they read against the chemical; wireframe seam guides dimmed violet. Contour segments touching a canvas edge are redrawn shifted by the wrap so closed loops read continuously across the weld instead of chopping off. v2.3.1: operator-reported 3D misalignment (left planes not lining up) — root cause: the v2.2.0 texture/relief path folded the uv a second time (guessing the parametrization needed the sim's mirror), but the surface parametrization already IS the folded immersion; the extra fold split the texture along a line the geometry never folds. foldUv is now the identity — the gluing lives in the parametrization and the sim-side foldRead, exactly once each. v2.3.2: Codex co-review (gpt-6-astra, read-only) confirmed the operator's residual 3D misalignment was a VERTICAL TEXTURE FLIP — three.js CanvasTexture defaults flipY=true, so texture rows ran opposite to the height sampling rows. Fixed with flipY=false. Two follow-on defects from the same review: entities (contours, agent points) now ride the ACTUAL displaced mesh via barycentric interpolation instead of the analytic surface (they floated/sank between mesh vertices), and relief 0 now restores base positions instead of freezing the last displacement. v2.3.3: hardened the overlay against a devicePixelRatio desync — the canvas is sized and transformed with the DPR live at fit time, but the draw paths re-read devicePixelRatio, and a window dragged to a display of different pixel density changes it without firing resize. Scale is now committed once per fit (ovSX/ovSY), a matchMedia (resolution: Ndppx) listener refits on density change, and a ResizeObserver on the sim panel covers layout changes that never resize the window. NOTE: this was a real latent defect but NOT the cause of the operator's report — see v2.3.4. v2.3.4: the actual cause of the operator-reported quarter-size overlay — drawContours computed the grid→CSS scale and then never applied it. buildContour emits paths in GRID units (0..W) because segStore is reused for the 3D push, so the strokes must carry the scale themselves; without it contours drew one grid unit per CSS pixel, filling a W-sized patch in the top-left of an s-sized box. The error is W/s, so it is invisible when the sim panel is about W wide and grows with the window — which is why it read as 'quarter size' on a wide window and looked fine on a narrow one. Strokes now run under octx.scale(sx,sy) with line widths divided back out so the authored weights hold; segStore stays in grid units for the 3D push. The test port exposes __welded.ovScale so the registration can be measured rather than eyeballed. Verified at a 1355x760 viewport: violet contour centroid (0.711, 0.518) against field centroid (0.716, 0.527) on the sim canvas — agreement to within 0.01 of the canvas, where the pre-fix overlay centroid sat at (0.336, 0.334) against a field centroid of (0.500, 0.498). v2.4.0: the 3D shell is now a declared render mode — translucent (new default), wireframe, or solid. A closed quotient surface occludes its own far side, so the opaque shell hid exactly what the panel exists to show: the loops, contours and agents on the back of the torus, and the figure-8 Klein's pass-through entirely. The lever is depthWrite, not opacity — a transparent shell that still writes depth hides everything behind it however see-through it looks; translucent and wireframe both drop depthWrite so the whole shape reads at once. The mode is reapplied on every surface rebuild and is drivable from the test port via __welded.setShell(), with state().shell reporting it. v2.5.0: the sim became runnable as an experiment rather than only watchable. The physics was inside the rAF callback, so it advanced only while the page was painted — a hidden tab froze it and a run's length was wall-clock, not step count. simStep() is now the unit of time and loop() is one simStep plus one paint. Every stochastic draw goes through a seeded stream (mulberry32), spawn can be 'disc' (the ancestor's, still the interactive default) or 'uniform', and the test port gains pause/resume/step(n) plus run(spec) — {seed, surface, spawn, params, at:{step:{...}}, steps} — which returns a manifest that replays identically. PARAMETERS ARE PINNED TO THE TIMELINE: a change is declared at a step index, fires exactly once there, is recorded in the manifest, and drives the slider so the panel cannot show 60 degrees while the sim runs at 90. A run mutated by hand mid-flight is not reproducible, which is how a reported state became unrecoverable. Verified: identical seed reproduces the grid bit-for-bit, a different seed does not, a scheduled change alters the outcome and still replays, and stepping runs at full CPU with the page hidden. v2.5.1: three code paths disagreed about which axis a mirrored weld flips. topo.<axis>.flip NAMES the mirroring axis — Klein is y:{flip:'x'}, so crossing the y-seam mirrors x. wrapPos (agent re-entry) and diffuseDecay's nbT (trail diffusion) read it that way; foldRead mirrored the CROSSED axis instead, so an agent sensing past the weld read the field from a point its own deposits never reach, and momRead flipped vx — per its own comment, which states the correct rule — while folding the coordinate in y. Verified at (40, H+10) on the Klein: re-entry (260,10) and diffusion (259,10) against sensing (40,289). foldRead now honours the named axis; __welded.ablate({seamFold:'legacy'}) reproduces the old path as a control. MEASURED AND NEGATIVE: this does NOT remove the Klein seam accumulation. Uniform spawn, seeds 11 and 22, 4000 steps, both arms end at 11-12.5x the uniform expectation for the rows either side of the weld, against 0.0-0.3 on the torus control. The inconsistency was real; it is not the cause of the accumulation, which remains unexplained and may be genuine dynamics — a mirror line is a natural condensation locus for a physarum network. v2.6.0: slice scope — a planar section of the torus at height c cuts the surface in two circles; the trail is sampled on both and their per-theta difference is normalized by the clamped dimensional radius rho_c = R + sqrt(max(0, r^2 - c^2)), the section's actual radial reach. The diff profile encodes the plane the physarum structure lives on: flat ~0 means toroidally uniform, +mean is an outer-wall (equator-like) loop, -mean a bore (polar) loop, and a sinusoidal diff is a tilted/Villarceau-like band whose first-Fourier phase reveals the plane's orientation and whose amplitude the off-plane share. Panel: z slider, hi/lo/diff strip chart, live rho_c, Delta-bar/rho_c, amp and phase readouts; also exposed on the test port as __welded.slice(). v2.7.0: quadrant scope + gyroscopic readout — two orthogonal planes through the torus axis carve the ring into four quarter-sections whose trail masses are live (the 'clean quarter slice'). The torus provides the reference frame: the field's center of mass is computed every frame directly from the grid, mapped through the embedding to xyz, and reported in toroidal coordinates — rho (radial offset from the central ring), z, and omega, the per-step precession rate of the COM about the axis (frame-to-frame theta difference). The quadrant panel shows the ring from above with cutting planes, quarter-mass arc thickness, the COM marker displaced by rho, and a 120-step precession trace. Balanced ring = COM on axis, omega ~ 0; a tilted off-axis structure shows a nonzero rho with a precessing theta — the gyroscopic reading. On the test port: __welded.com(), __welded.quadrants(). v2.8.0: collector plates — the four quarter-sections reframed as accelerator pickup electrodes (beam-position monitor): the readout is the normalized difference b = (b_x, b_y) = ((Q_R - Q_L)/(sum), (Q_U - Q_D)/(sum)) in [-1,1]^2, which divides out total trail intensity entirely. |b| is how off-axis the field's mass sits, atan2(b_y, b_x) is the steering angle (the precession angle in BPM dress), and the trace of (b_x, b_y) over time is the precession plot — total-charge-free and comparable across runs. The panel shows the four plates at the rim brightening by collected charge, the steering vector on a crosshair, and a 180-step trace. Balanced beam reads (0,0) at any brightness; a beam hugging one plate reads toward +-1. On the test port: __welded.plates(). v2.9.0: mobile/fold experience — the 3D pane takes touch-action:none so one-finger drag orbits instead of scrolling the page, plus two-pointer pinch zoom (distance delta drives camera distance, pointer capture per pointer, cancel-safe). On narrow or coarse-pointer screens the three fixed panels (sidebar | sim | 3D) become a stacked tabbed stage: a two-tab bar (sim / 3D) switches which pane is full-width, and the control sidebar becomes a slide-in drawer behind a fixed hamburger toggle. Desktop layout untouched (media query only). v2.10.0: Villarceau scope — the third slice family as an instrument. A plane tilted alpha from the equator cuts the torus in a loop pair whose topology flips at the critical angle sin(alpha*) = r/R (26.74 deg on the sim's R=1, r=0.45 embedding): separate pair below, exact tangent (Villarceau, linked circles) at, interlaced pair above. The scope solves the section condition per tube angle (n-hat . torusXYZ(u,v) = d is linear in cos u, sin u -> 0/1/2 roots), samples the trail on both branch curves, and reads per-v traces plus first-harmonic amp/phase and a loop-correlation 'link' scalar that climbs toward 1 as the loops merge (measured: 0 at alpha=0, 0.89 at alpha=85). The obliquity dial is free 0-90 deg with the critical angle and live regime (separate/tangent/interlaced) labeled on the panel — the obliquity of the slicing plane is itself a probe coordinate, completing the multidimensional-oscilloscope chart alongside the equatorial slice scope and the axial quadrant scope. Design doc: docs/villarceau-scope.md. Verified headless: regime classification flips exactly at alpha*, 0 page errors, port __welded.vill()/VLS.
